findings.issue: Non-UTF-8 target values bypass whitespace trimming. For inline or separated Unix target bytes `20 62 61 64 ff 20`, Rust quotes `" bad\xff "`; frozen Go resolveTargets applies strings.TrimSpace first and quotes `"bad\xff"`. This is a source-confirmed stderr parity defect; the existing raw-byte probes contain no surrounding whitespace.
findings.fix: Trim target values with Go-compatible, byte-preserving whitespace semantics before validation and quoting. Extend the existing raw-value regression to cover padded invalid UTF-8 targets in both inline and separated forms. Keep scope diagnostics untrimmed, matching Go.
